statements.worth_reason: An exploratory partnership with a pre-revenue nuclear startup is at most a low-weight datapoint on power-constrained AI siting; it cannot move NVIDIA's revenue.
statements.day_note: 2026-07-01 is supported: the collaboration was announced 'on Wednesday afternoon' and 2026-07-01 is a Wednesday.

statements.worth_reason: Same announcement as e1 with the 30 MW size; one matter told in several sentences is one record, and the size belonged in e1.
Valar's own reactor milestone (100 kW) has no bearing on NVIDIA or on AI power supply at any relevant scale.
A third telling of the same 30 MW exploration ('exploring the deployment of a 30 megawatt data center').
Restates NVIDIA's already announced DSX design ('recently announced', no date, no number); product detail without business scale.
A product specification (water kept at 113°F); the standard's product-detail row.
A background licensing requirement for Valar's reactor; no bearing on NVIDIA.
An NRC chair's aim to cut reactor licensing to under 18 months bears on how fast nuclear power can feed AI data centres, but it is a hope, not a decided step, and far from NVIDIA's revenue.

grade_reason: No field is wrong and dates are handled honestly, but a 30 MW exploratory announcement becomes eight records: three tell the same partnership, and four (reactor criticality, DSX recap, water temperature, NRC licence requirement) are noise for NVIDIA. The useful content is one record (e1 with e2's size) and perhaps e8; no question, correctly.
standard_doubt: '有名有姓的动作缺金额、缺日期也照留' (D240) together with '没有量的"在谈""在考虑""可能""在探索""打算"不算' (6, 确定状态): the second sentence only keeps an exploration out of core, so the standard still keeps a 'partnership to explore' with a pre-revenue startup as supporting evidence; an analyst covering NVIDIA would treat a 30 MW 'considering/exploring' release as noise.
